subject: PayFlux: checkout gap bucketization and proposed remedy path
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria@payflux.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: PayFlux SRE <sre@payflux.com>
Date: 2028-06-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: intermittent checkout failures 2028-06-13 22:40-23:05 PT - immediate SLA clarification request

Hi Karthik / Laura,

We observed a series of transient failures hitting our checkout flow last night between 22:40 and 23:05 PT (timestamps attached). ~12% of checkout attempts returned 502/timeout-like responses; some retried successfully. For billing and reconciliation purposes we need a deterministic confirmation from Redwood about: (1) whether that interval qualifies as "downtime" under our SLO definition, and (2) if eligible, the calculation method you will use to allocate credit (minute-level, per-tenant apportionment, etc.).

Attached: payflux-error-samples.log and a CSV with per-request timestamps (payflux-purchase-timeline.csv). We can provide more slices if helpful.

This is time-sensitive for our finance team — they asked for an initial eligibility check today and a postmortem schedule for this week if applicable. Please advise next steps and what evidence you require.

Thanks,
Maria Gomez
Head of Platform Reliability, PayFlux

--
Attachment: payflux-error-samples.log (text, 82KB)
Attachment: payflux-purchase-timeline.csv (csv, 24KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Maria Gomez <maria@payflux.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-14T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: intermittent checkout failures 2028-06-13 22:40-23:05 PT - immediate SLA clarification request

Hi Maria — thanks for the heads-up and for the attached artifacts. We’ve started an initial triage. Quick answers up-front: we’ll run the interval against the contractual SLO (availability measured by minute-bucket success rate) and return an eligibility determination by EOD.

To make that determination we need:
- a short list of representative request IDs (3–5) for failed vs successful attempts around 22:50 so we can correlate tenant routing and shard mapping;
- any BizOps-relevant revenue windows (if some failed requests are outside billable checkout windows we may exclude them from proportional crediting);
- confirmation whether PayFlux wants minute-level bucketization (preferred) or second-level aggregation (nonstandard, will require reprocessing).

Aditya — looping you in to flag this as a potential SLO adjudication; could you pull the per-minute availability digest for the US-WEST region for 22:30–23:10 PT and start a provisional apportionment calc?

I’ll collect traces and forward the raw trace bundle and a short timeline once we have the correlated IDs. If the interval meets the SLA threshold for relief, we’ll propose a prorated credit calculation and invite PayFlux to a postmortem Tuesday.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Maria Gomez <maria@payflux.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: PayFlux SRE <sre@payflux.com>
Date: 2028-06-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: intermittent checkout failures 2028-06-13 22:40-23:05 PT - immediate SLA clarification request

Thanks Karthik — attaching a short list of three failed request IDs and three succeeding ones around 22:49–22:52. We do expect minute-level bucketization; second-level would be noisy for our accounting.

Notes: our finance window includes all transactions between 22:00–23:59 PT, so please include that in any proportionalization calculations. We’ll also share a short Doc with transaction values if you need dollar-weighted apportionment.

Attached now: payflux-purchase-timeline.csv (updated) and a short trace excerpt (in comments in the CSV).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Maria

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Maria Gomez <maria@payflux.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-14T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: intermittent checkout failures 2028-06-13 22:40-23:05 PT - immediate SLA clarification request

Maria — I pulled the per-minute availability digest and correlated PayFlux request IDs to shard ownership. High-level provisional findings:
- US-WEST minute buckets: 22:40–22:44 = 99.95% availability; 22:45 = 98.2%; 22:46–22:50 had a cluster of short-lived 502s that pushed 22:47 and 22:48 down to ~91% (these are the critical minutes).
- The 22:47 and 22:48 minute buckets meet our definition of an availability breach per the SLO described in section 3.1 of the SLO terms.

Proposed credit approach (initial):
1) Minute-level bucketization as requested.
2) Pro-rated credit by (number of breached minutes)/(total minutes in billing window) * monthly committed fee, then apportioned by tenant weight using transaction counts.
3) If PayFlux prefers revenue-weighted split instead of transaction-count weighting, we can re-run once you share the small Doc with transaction values.

Next steps: I’ll assemble the raw trace bundle and an internal timeline and circulate a proposed credit calculation tomorrow AM. Can we tentatively schedule a 60-minute postmortem review on Tuesday 2028-06-20 at 10:00 PT?

— Aditya Rao
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: slo-terms-extract.pdf (pdf, 18KB)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Maria Gomez <maria@payflux.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-15T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: intermittent checkout failures 2028-06-13 22:40-23:05 PT - immediate SLA clarification request

Maria — confirming Redwood will treat minute-level bucketization as the primary adjudication method (per contract). We agree with Aditya’s provisional finding that 22:47 and 22:48 qualify as breached minutes under section 3.1.

Action items we’ll own:
- Finalize the evidence bundle (raw traces + host-level metrics) and share by COB tomorrow.
- Produce a provisional credit calc using transaction-count weighting; we’ll re-run for revenue-weighted if you send the values.
- Schedule a postmortem for 2028-06-20 10:00 PT; calendar invite to follow.

If PayFlux would like a faster decision on the credit amount (for invoicing), reply with "approve provisional credit" and we can issue a provisional credit pending final trace reconciliation.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
